newsitem.title: FRANCE: Argentine Navy finds no sign of missing Canadian.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Navy finds no sign of missing Canadian.

text.p: Searches by the Argentine and Chilean navies on both sides of Cape Horn have failed to find any sign of Canadian Gerry Roufs, missing on a round-the-world yacht race, the French sea rescue service said on Tuesday.
It said an Argentine Navy patrolboat was keeping up the search of the southern tip of south America, exploring possible moorings in the Beagle Channel and States Island.
The search would be dropped on Wednesday if nothing was found by then, the rescue service which is coordinating the search for Roufs from western France said in a statement.
It said the Chilean Navy planes flew five search missions last week after a Chilean aircraft made a brief radio contact in the Pacific Ocean west of Cape Horn with a boat that might have been Roufs'.
Argentine planes made three unsuccessful searches of the Atlantic area between Cape Horn and the Falklands Islands.
Roufs, a competitor in the Vendee Globe race, has been missing for nearly two weeks. His last known position was 1,500 miles (2,400 km) west of Cape Horn in the South Pacific.

The French rescue service said Roufs could either be making for the Chilean coast with a makeshift rig and would arrive next month, or he was sailing normally with his communications down and was already in the Atlantic.
Another possibility was that his capsized boat was drifting in the South Pacific, and there was little chance that Roufs could still be alive in dire weather conditions.
